summary: Keep the total of a window of K days and slide it one day at a time: add the new day, drop the oldest (T12 — sliding window). Each slide is O(1), so we never re-add K numbers.

blocks.title: Read N, K and the sales
blocks.text: N and K are on ONE line, so split them. Sales come on the next line.

blocks.title: The first window
blocks.text: `sum(sales[:K])` is days 1..K. `best` starts at this window, NOT at 0 — sales can be negative, so the true best total might be below 0.

blocks.title: Slide the window
blocks.text: Moving one day right adds `sales[i]` and removes `sales[i - K]`, the day that just left the window. Keep the maximum. If K = N the loop never runs and the first window is the answer.

complexity: Time O(N) with N ≤ 10⁵ — instant. Re-summing every window would be O(N·K), up to 10¹⁰.
pitfalls: Starting `best` at 0 when all sales are negative.
